Algebra I · Lesson 3.1

The Laws of Exponents with Variables

Solve this lesson →All lessons

1.5 built the exponent laws out of counting, and every one of those counts still works when the base is a letter. A letter stands for a number you have not named yet, so k5k5 is five factors of kk. What is new is knowing when the laws do not apply. There are two such cases, powers with different bases and terms joined by a plus sign.

Problem
m3⋅m⋅m4m3⋅m⋅m4 is a row of factors of mm with nothing but multiplication in it. Written as a single power it is mkmk. Count the factors and enter kk.
Show a hint
  • Write out the factors of mm in each piece, then count the whole row.
  • A letter with no exponent written is one factor.
Show the full solution
A letter with no exponent written is one factor, since m=m1m=m1, so the row is 3 factors then 1 then 4. Joining rows adds the counts, giving 88​. Skipping the bare mm is the easy miss and gives 7.
Key idea
The product rule. The product rule from 1.5 is xm⋅xn=xm+nxm⋅xn=xm+n, and it still holds because the count does not depend on the base. Two mistakes are common. a3⋅a4a3⋅a4 is a7a7 and not a12a12, because exponents count factors, and combining them adds the counts instead of multiplying them. It is also not 2a72a7, because the two powers were multiplied, not added.
Problem
A student writes n2+n5=n7n2+n5=n7, adding the exponents. Test the claim by picking a number, the way 1.4 did. Evaluate n2+n5n2+n5 at n=2n=2 and enter the value.
Show a hint
  • n2n2 and n5n5 are separate terms, so work out each one and then add.
  • For comparison, n7n7 at n=2n=2 is 128.
Show the full solution
At n=2n=2, n2=4n2=4 and n5=32n5=32, so n2+n5=4+32=36n2+n5=4+32=36​. The claim predicts n7=128n7=128, and one mismatch kills it. The product rule applies to a product, and this is a sum.
Key idea
Two conditions. The laws need a shared base, and they need multiplication. a3b4a3b4 has two different bases, so there is no single power equal to it. a3+a4a3+a4 is not a7a7 either. A plus sign joins terms, not factors, and a3a3 and a4a4 are not like terms in the 2.4 sense. Both expressions are already as short as they get.
Problem
Multiply (4c5)(7c3)(4c5)(7c3) into a single term. The numbers out front and the powers of cc do not get the same treatment, so decide what happens to each before you write anything. Enter the result, typed like 6y26y2.
Show a hint
  • Gather the numbers together and the cc factors together, the 1.3 way.
  • The 4 and the 7 are factors. The 5 and the 3 are counts.
Show the full solution
Coefficients are factors, so they multiply, 4⋅7=284⋅7=28. Exponents are counts, so they add, 5+3=85+3=8. The term is 28c828c8​. Treating both halves alike gives 28c1528c15 or 11c811c8, each applying the wrong operation to half the term.
Key idea
Monomial products. A number multiplied by powers of letters is called a monomial. A coefficient is one more factor, so the reordering from 1.3 lets you gather numbers with numbers and letters with letters. In (3a4)(5a2)(3a4)(5a2) the 3 and the 5 are factors, so they get multiplied. The 4 and the 2 are counts, so they get added. The term is 15a615a6.
Problem
In z11z4z4z11​, every factor on the bottom cancels a matching factor on top. What remains is a single power zkzk. Enter kk.
Show a hint
  • Four factors cancel four factors. How many of the eleven are left?
Show the full solution
The four factors on the bottom cancel four of the eleven on top, so 11−4=711−4=7​ factors survive. The 4 is the count that got cancelled, not the count left over.
Problem
Simplify 54k106k36k354k10​ to a single term. The number part and the kk part are handled separately. Enter the coefficient of the result.
Show a hint
  • Split it into a number part and a kk part.
  • The coefficients divide. Only the exponents subtract.
Show the full solution
The coefficients divide, 54÷6=954÷6=9, and the exponents subtract, 10−3=710−3=7, so the term is 9k79k7 and the coefficient is 99​. Subtraction belongs to the exponents. Subtracting the numbers out front would give 48.
Key idea
The quotient rule. The quotient rule from 1.5 also holds for letters, xmxn=xm−nxnxm​=xm−n. Each factor on the bottom cancels one on top, and the exponent left is the count that remains. With coefficients there are two steps. The numbers divide and the counts subtract, so 20a74a3=5a44a320a7​=5a4. Keep the larger exponent on top for now. 3.2 removes that restriction.
Problem
(r4)6(r4)6 means six copies of r4r4 multiplied together. Written as one power it is rkrk. Count the factors of rr in that whole product and enter kk.
Show a hint
  • Each copy of r4r4 contributes four factors of rr.
Show the full solution
Each of the six copies of r4r4 brings four factors of rr, so the total is 4⋅6=244⋅6=24​. The 6 counts copies of a four-factor block, not extra factors, so adding to get 10 uses the product rule where it does not apply.
Key idea
Power of a power. (xm)n=xmn(xm)n=xmn. The outer exponent counts copies of the whole power, not extra factors. Multiplying two powers combines their factors, so the counts add. Raising a power repeats the whole power, so the counts multiply. This is why a4⋅a3a4⋅a3 is a7a7 while (a4)3(a4)3 is a12a12.
Problem
Both q5⋅q4q5⋅q4 and (q5)4(q5)4 collapse to a single power of qq, and they do not collapse the same way. Write each one as a single power of qq. Take the exponent on qq in the collapsed form of (q5)4(q5)4 and subtract the exponent on qq in the collapsed form of q5⋅q4q5⋅q4. Enter that one number.
Show a hint
  • One expression sets two rows side by side. The other makes four copies of one row.
  • 5+45+4 and 5⋅45⋅4 are not the same number.
Show the full solution
Side by side adds the counts, so q5⋅q4=q9q5⋅q4=q9. Four copies multiply them, so (q5)4=q20(q5)4=q20. The difference is 20−9=1120−9=11​. Reading the two as the same thing gives 0, which is exactly the confusion.
Problem
Expand (3b7)3(3b7)3 into a single term. The outer exponent makes three copies of everything inside the parentheses, the 3 in front included. Enter the coefficient of the result.
Show a hint
  • Write the three copies out. What sits inside each one?
Show the full solution
Three copies of 3b73b7 hold three 3s and twenty-one bbs, so the term is 27b2127b21 and the coefficient is 2727​. The outer exponent reaches the coefficient too, so 3b213b21 keeps only one of those three 3s.
Key idea
Power of a product. (cam)n=cnamn(cam)n=cnamn. The outer exponent makes nn copies of the whole term, and the coefficient is inside every copy, so it gets raised too. (2a3)4(2a3)4 is four copies of 2a32a3, which gives four 2s and twelve aas, so it is 16a1216a12. Writing 2a122a12 keeps only one of those four 2s. This is the rule (ab)n=anbn(ab)n=anbn from 1.5 with a number in place of one letter.
Problem
Expand (u3w8)4(u3w8)4. Each base carries its own exponent through the expansion. Enter the exponent on ww in the result.
Show a hint
  • Four copies of u3w8u3w8 reorder into all the uu factors and then all the ww factors.
Show the full solution
Every copy of u3w8u3w8 contains eight ww factors, so four copies give u12w32u12w32 and the exponent on ww is 3232​. The outer 4 reaches both bases. Applying it to the first one only leaves w8w8 untouched.
Key idea
Each base gets its own exponent. (xmyn)k=xmkynk(xmyn)k=xmkynk. Reordering the copies by 1.3 groups all the xx factors together and all the yy factors together, and the exponent on one base never changes the other. That also fixes the order of work for a mixed expression. Clear every parenthesis first with the power rules, then multiply across the top, then cancel.
Problem
Simplify (2y4)3⋅5y2(2y4)3⋅5y2 to a single term. Clear the parentheses first, then multiply. Enter the result, typed like 6k56k5.
Show a hint
  • The cube reaches the 2 as well as the y4y4.
  • Once the parentheses are gone it is one product of two monomials.
Show the full solution
The cube makes three copies of 2y42y4, so the parentheses clear to 8y128y12. Then 8⋅5=408⋅5=40 and 12+2=1412+2=14, giving 40y1440y14​. Skipping the 2323 gives 10y1410y14, which is the whole trap.
Problem
Simplify (5f4)2⋅f35f65f6(5f4)2⋅f3​ to a single term, then evaluate that term at f=2f=2. Enter the value, a single number.
Show a hint
  • Clear the parentheses first, then build one term on top before you divide.
  • Check what the outside exponent does to the 5, not just to f4f4.
Show the full solution
(5f4)2=25f8(5f4)2=25f8, so the top is 25f8⋅f3=25f1125f8⋅f3=25f11. Dividing by 5f65f6 gives 5f55f5, and at f=2f=2 that is 5⋅32=1605⋅32=160​. The outside exponent reaches the 5 as well as the f4f4, so 5f85f8 is not enough.
Fun fact
The word exponent is older than the symbol. Michael Stifel coined it in 1544, lining the powers of 2 up beside their exponents and noticing that multiplying in one column matched adding in the other. Logarithms grew from that.

Every exponent in this lesson was a positive whole number, and we kept it that way by putting the larger exponent on top of every quotient. 3.2 drops that rule. Once the bottom exponent is allowed to be the larger one, x0x0 and x−3x−3 need a meaning, and the meaning is whatever keeps these laws working.

Practice these ideas

Practice
Write g7⋅g8g7⋅g8 as a single power gkgk and enter kk.
Show the solution
Joining two rows of gg factors adds the counts, 7+8=157+8=15​. Multiplying the exponents would give g56g56, which counts copies that are not there.
Practice
A student claims d2+d4=d6d2+d4=d6. Test it the 1.4 way. Evaluate d2+d4d2+d4 at d=3d=3 and enter the value.
Show the solution
At d=3d=3, d2=9d2=9 and d4=81d4=81, so the value is 9+81=909+81=90​. The claim predicts 36=72936=729, so it fails. A plus sign joins terms, not rows of factors.
Practice
A student claims a4b2=(ab)6a4b2=(ab)6. Test the claim by evaluating a4b2a4b2 at a=2a=2 and b=3b=3, and enter the value.
Show the solution
At a=2a=2 and b=3b=3, a4b2=16⋅9=144a4b2=16⋅9=144​. The claim would give 66=4665666=46656, so it fails. Adding exponents needs a shared base, and aa and bb are different bases.
Practice
Multiply (7h2)(2h6)(7h2)(2h6) into a single term and enter its coefficient.
Show the solution
7⋅2=147⋅2=14, so the term is 14h814h8 and the coefficient is 1414​. The exponents have nothing to do with the coefficient.
Practice
Multiply (8p3)(3p4)(8p3)(3p4) into a single term. Enter the result, typed like 5y25y2.
Show the solution
Coefficients multiply, 8⋅3=248⋅3=24, while exponents add, 3+4=73+4=7, giving 24p724p7​. Adding the coefficients to get 11p711p7 is the tempting slip, but they are factors, not terms.
Practice
Simplify v16v6v6v16​ to a single power vkvk and enter kk.
Show the solution
Six factors on the bottom cancel six of the sixteen on top, so 16−6=1016−6=10​ factors of vv are still standing. Answering 6 reports the count that cancels, not the exponent left behind.
Practice
Simplify 48t96t46t448t9​ to a single term. Enter it, typed like 3y23y2.
Show the solution
The coefficients divide, 48÷6=848÷6=8, and the counts subtract, 9−4=59−4=5, giving 8t58t5​. Carrying the 48 along and only subtracting the exponents leaves the number part untouched.
Practice
(s6)7(s6)7 is seven copies of s6s6 multiplied together. Write it as sksk and enter kk.
Show the solution
Each of the seven copies contributes six factors of ss, so the row holds 6⋅7=426⋅7=42​ factors. Adding the exponents gives 13, but that is the product rule, and this is a power raised to a power.
Practice
Expand (5n3)3(5n3)3 into a single term and enter its coefficient.
Show the solution
The outer exponent applies to every factor inside the parentheses, so (5n3)3=53⋅n3⋅3=125n9(5n3)3=53⋅n3⋅3=125n9 and the coefficient is 125125​. Leaving the 5 alone gives 5n95n9 and drops two of the three 5s.
Practice
Simplify each of (c3)8(c3)8 and c3⋅c8c3⋅c8 to a single power of cc. Enter the exponent of the first minus the exponent of the second.
Show the solution
Stacking eight copies of c3c3 multiplies the counts, so (c3)8=c24(c3)8=c24. Setting two rows side by side adds them, so c3⋅c8=c11c3⋅c8=c11. The difference is 24−11=1324−11=13​. Reading both the same way gives 0.
Practice
Expand (j5z3)3(j5z3)3 and enter the exponent on zz.
Show the solution
Each of the three copies carries three zz factors, so the result is j15z9j15z9 and the exponent on zz is 99​. The 3 outside reaches both letters, not just the first one.
Practice
Simplify (2m5)48m118m11(2m5)4​ to a single term. Enter it, typed like 7v37v3.
Show the solution
The parentheses clear to 16m2016m20, then 16÷8=216÷8=2 and 20−11=920−11=9, giving 2m92m9​. Forgetting 2424 leaves 2m202m20 on top and wrecks the coefficient.
